steps.title: Thaw and seed HeLa cells
steps.instruction: Quickly thaw a cryotube of HeLa Kyoto cells in a warm water bath, add the cells to a T‑75 flask containing 10 mL pre‑warmed DMEM‑WT (DMEM + GlutaMax, 1×, supplemented with 9.01 % v/v FBS and 0.9 % v/v Penicillin/Streptomycin), incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, humidified for 1 day, then replace medium with fresh pre‑warmed DMEM‑WT; passage 2–3 times until cells reach ~70 % confluency the day before the experiment.

steps.title: Clean 3D‑printed chambers
steps.instruction: Wash the custom‑printed incubation chambers with 70 % (v/v) ethanol, let dry, and store them in a humidified incubator at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until use.

steps.title: Clean sapphire discs
steps.instruction: Place all sapphire discs (Ø 3 mm) into a glass beaker containing acetone, gently mix for 5–10 min, remove with fine tweezers, rinse twice in three dishes of ddH₂O, then once in 70 % (v/v) ethanol, store discs in an Eppendorf tube containing 70 % ethanol until coating.

steps.title: Coat sapphire discs with poly‑L‑lysine
steps.instruction: Air‑dry discs for 1 h in a closed Petri dish, then apply a single drop of 0.1 % (w/v) poly‑L‑lysine in ddH₂O to each disc, incubate 5 min under the dish, blot excess with filter paper, place discs on a heating plate at 60 °C for 2 h, then cool in a closed Petri dish (use a slightly sticky rubber pad to prevent sticking).

steps.title: Coat discs with fibronectin
steps.instruction: Prepare fresh 10 % (v/v) fibronectin solution by diluting fibronectin 1:10 in 1× PBS, gently mix, apply a drop to each poly‑L‑lysine‑coated disc, incubate 10 min at room temperature, remove droplet with a pipette, place discs into the 3D‑printed chambers and store in the cell‑culture incubator (37 °C, 5 % CO₂) until use.

steps.title: Synchronize cells by mitotic shake‑off
steps.instruction: Warm complete DMEM‑WT medium to 37 °C and leave open in the incubator for CO₂ equilibration. One day before the experiment move all T‑75 flasks to the room of the high‑pressure freezer. To synchronize, remove a flask, hit its bottom firmly on a bench, discard the medium (containing dead/mitotic cells), add 5 mL pre‑warmed medium, discard, add 10 mL fresh pre‑warmed medium and return to the incubator for 2 h. Repeat for additional flasks at 15–20 min intervals if needed. After 2 h, repeat the hit, collect the entire medium (containing mitotic cells) with a 15 mL pipette into a 15 mL Falcon tube, centrifuge at 0.2 × g for 5 min at 37 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 1 mL pre‑warmed medium, and immediately add the suspension to the fibronectin‑coated sapphire discs in the 3D‑printed chamber. Incubate the chamber at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 10–15 min to allow cell re‑attachment.

steps.title: Assemble high‑pressure freezing sandwich
steps.instruction: Warm a metal heating block to 37 °C, place the 3D‑printed chamber with discs on it, under a stereomicroscope place an aluminum planchette (40 µm cavity) inside the sample holder, add 1 µL pre‑warmed DMEM‑HPF solution (see recipe) into the cavity, dip each sapphire disc (cells facing down) into the solution, flip the disc so cells face the carrier, gently place the disc onto the aluminum carrier ensuring no air bubbles, close the holder and freeze immediately using the Wohlwend Compact 03 high‑pressure freezer. Retrieve the frozen sandwich under liquid nitrogen, press the back of the holder with a cold tweezer to release the sapphire disc into a cryo‑tube, keep specimens submerged in LN₂ and store until freeze‑substitution.

steps.title: Prepare methylene‑blue‑saturated acetone
steps.instruction: Add 5 g methylene blue powder to 60 mL anhydrous, glass‑distilled acetone (room temperature), shake to mix, close bottle and store at –80 °C overnight, then filter the solution through a 0.2 µm syringe filter.

steps.title: Prepare AFS freeze‑substitution cocktail
steps.instruction: To the filtered methylene‑blue‑saturated acetone add 0.5 g osmium tetroxide (1 % w/v) and 0.05 g uranyl acetate (0.1 % w/v) to obtain a total volume of 50 mL; aliquot 1 mL into 2 mL cryo‑tubes, freeze immediately in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C until use.

steps.title: Freeze‑substitution of frozen sandwiches
steps.instruction: Under liquid nitrogen open each high‑pressure‑frozen sandwich, transfer the sapphire disc into a 2 mL cryo‑vial containing 1 mL of the AFS cocktail, then place the vials into an automated freeze‑substitution machine. Run the program: hold at –90 °C for 1 h; warm to –30 °C at 5 °C h⁻¹; hold at –30 °C for 5 h; warm to 0 °C at 5 °C h⁻¹; at 0 °C remove discs (do not exceed 1 h at 0 °C).

steps.title: Wash and transfer discs to acetone
steps.instruction: Wash each disc once with pure anhydrous acetone at room temperature inside the cryo‑vial, then move the disc to a glass Petri dish filled with anhydrous acetone, keep the disc immersed and orient cells face up under a binocular microscope.

steps.title: Infiltrate with resin – step 1
steps.instruction: Place each disc into a round flow‑through ring (Leica) inside a plastic reagent bath, pre‑fill the mold with a 1:3 (v/v) mixture of Epon/Araldite resin (see recipe) and acetone to keep the disc wet.

steps.title: Infiltrate with resin – step 2
steps.instruction: Fill each mold to at least three‑quarters with the same 1:3 resin/acetone mixture, then sequentially infiltrate at room temperature with increasing resin/acetone ratios: 1:3 (v/v) for 1 h, 1:1 (v/v) for 1 h, and 3:1 (v/v) for 1 h, performing each exchange very slowly to avoid disc detachment.

steps.title: Embed in pure resin and polymerize
steps.instruction: Fill the molds completely with pure Epon/Araldite resin, incubate at room temperature overnight (ensure no meniscus), then polymerize at 60 °C for at least 48 h in an oven.

steps.title: Release resin‑embedded cells from sapphire
steps.instruction: Cut the plastic molds open with a scalpel or Dremel, break the resin blocks out with a desmotome VT1 and hammer, under an ultramicrotome remove resin around the sapphire disc with a single‑edge razor blade, submerge only the top part of the resin block containing the disc in liquid nitrogen for a few seconds, press the disc edge against a heated razor blade (≈ heated) to release the disc, collect the disc; if release fails after 2–3 attempts, repeat resin removal around the disc.

steps.title: Pre‑screen resin block for mitotic cells
steps.instruction: Place the resin block (cells side facing up) on a 24 mm × 60 mm coverslip on a glass slide, add a droplet of water, and examine under an upright transmitted‑light microscope or a fluorescence microscope (e.g., Leica SP5/SP8) using 594 nm excitation and 620–730 nm emission to detect methylene‑blue‑stained chromosomes. Locate rounded cells with condensed chromosomes, capture images at low and high magnifications, record coordinates for later relocation, and discard damaged cells.

steps.title: Trim resin block for serial sectioning
steps.instruction: Using a razor blade, perform a rough trim of the block around the region of interest, re‑locate the area under an upright bright‑field microscope, repeat trimming until the block face is a trapezoid of appropriate size for ultramicrotomy.

steps.title: Serial sectioning on ultramicrotome
steps.instruction: Mount the trimmed block on an ultramicrotome equipped with a diamond knife; overfill the knife boat with water, add 1–3 droplets of 70 % ethanol, remove excess water until a bright reflection appears at the knife edge. Cut 300 nm sections at a speed of 1.6 mm s⁻¹ (± 0.3 mm s⁻¹), collect ribbons on Formvar‑coated copper slot grids (2 mm oval slot) using hair glued to a toothpick (e.g., Dalmatian dog hair).

steps.title: Post‑stain grids with fiducials
steps.instruction: Immerse each grid in a droplet of 20 nm colloidal gold solution for 1 min, blot excess fluid with filter paper, air‑dry 1 min, wash in double‑distilled water for 1 min, air‑dry again, and store grids in a grid box.

steps.title: Initial TEM inspection
steps.instruction: Inspect the serial sections on a TEM operated at 80 kV to validate cell selection and correlate with the previously acquired fluorescence images.

steps.title: Acquire tilt series with SerialEM
steps.instruction: Load the grid into a tomography sample holder, insert into the TEM (300 kV, tilting stage), open SerialEM, create a new map, mark positions of cells of interest on each section, set eucentric height for each position, use the pre‑exposure feature to expose each position to 2 000 e⁻ Å⁻² at 60° tilt for 5 min (baking), then acquire a tilt series for each region at ± 60° with 1° increments at 4 700× magnification (a‑axis). Rotate the grid by 90° and repeat the acquisition for the b‑axis.

steps.title: Automatic tomogram reconstruction (IMOD)
steps.instruction: Open the etomo package of IMOD, switch to batch processing mode, load the automatic reconstruction script from https://github.com/RRobert92/Assit_Automatic_Tomogram_Flattening_IMOD (Kiewisz_Imod_batch_reconstruction.adoc), select raw tilt‑series files (a‑ and b‑axis pairs stored in separate folders), choose processing device (CPU/GPU), run the batch; if the run reports ‘completed’ proceed, otherwise troubleshoot the reported failure step.

steps.title: Post‑process reconstructed tomograms
steps.instruction: Trim the histogram and rotate each volume around the x‑axis in IMOD, then run the automatic flattening tool from https://github.com/Robert92/Assit_Automatic_Tomogram_Flattening_IMOD/blob/main/AAFT.bat, finally use the IMOD ‘newstack’ command to delete empty z‑planes that contain no image data.

steps.title: Semi‑automatic microtubule segmentation (Amira)
steps.instruction: Load a reconstructed tomogram into Amira (or AmiraZIBEdition), select the Cylinder Correlation tool, set microtubule template‑matching parameters as in the published recipe, click Apply to generate two intermediate files; then select the Trace Correlation Lines tool, load the two intermediate files as inputs, set tracing parameters, click Apply to produce a spatial‑graph file (.am) containing predicted microtubule tracks, and save the file.

steps.title: Manual correction of segmented tracks
steps.instruction: Open the filament tab in Amira, delete false‑positive tracks by selecting them and pressing D, add missing tracks by pressing C then T to place the first node on the microtubule centre, extend the track by pressing N while holding Ctrl and clicking along the filament, verify that each track’s ends match the filament ends by scrolling through Z‑planes, and repeat until all tracks are correct.

steps.title: Stitch serial sections (Amira)
steps.instruction: Open AmiraZIBEdition, create a SerialSectionStack tool, add all tomogram files and their corresponding spatial‑graph files (named consecutively, e.g., Tomogram_1.am, Tomogram_sg_1.am, …) from the same folder, for each border open the SerialSectionAligner, click Advanced, switch to Matching mode, set Slice quality to High and Warping quality to Maximum, then press Compute to obtain the alignment transformation matrix; repeat for every consecutive section until histograms no longer change, finally press Create (optionally deselect ‘crop to filament’) to generate a stitched tomogram volume and a stitched spatial‑graph file.

steps.title: Final correction of stitched microtubules
steps.instruction: Open the stitched spatial‑graph file in Amira, repeat the manual correction workflow (delete false positives, add missing tracks, verify ends) to ensure continuity across all sections.

steps.title: Prepare AFS cocktail (recipe summary)
steps.instruction: Oversaturate 60 mL glass‑distilled acetone with 5 g methylene blue, shake at room temperature, store bottle at –80 °C overnight, filter, then for each 50 mL of AFS cocktail add 0.5 g osmium tetroxide (1 % w/v) and 0.05 g uranyl acetate (0.1 % w/v). Aliquot 1 mL into 2 mL cryo‑tubes, freeze in liquid nitrogen, store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare DMEM‑HPF solution (recipe)
steps.instruction: Mix 1 g BSA (10 % w/v) with 10 mL DMEM‑WT to obtain 10 mL of high‑pressure‑freezing solution; store at 4 °C until use.

steps.title: Prepare Epon/Araldite resin (recipe)
steps.instruction: In a single‑use plastic beaker, mix 25 mL Embed 812, 15 mL Araldite 502, 55 mL DDSA, and 2.5 mL BDMA (total 97.5 mL) overnight with magnetic stirring; next day fill 10 mL syringes, seal with Parafilm, store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare fibronectin coating solution (recipe)
steps.instruction: Combine 0.1 mL fibronectin with 0.9 mL 1× PBS (total 1 mL).

steps.title: Prepare Formvar solution (recipe)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 g Formvar powder in 100 mL chloroform to obtain a 1 % (w/v) solution; store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare lead citrate post‑stain (recipe)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 2 g lead citrate in 50 mL double‑distilled water (0.4 % w/v); store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 10× PBS buffer (recipe)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 8.9 g Na₂HPO₄ (100 mM), 1.2 g KH₂PO₄ (18 mM), 40 g NaCl (1.37 M), and 1 g KCl (27 mM) in double‑distilled water to a final volume of 500 mL; store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare uranyl acetate post‑stain (recipe)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.2 g uranyl acetate (2 % w/v) in 10 mL methanol; store at room temperature.
